chunks.title: Primary Action
chunks.structure: High-contrast button with brand gradient, elevated shadow and concise single label. Optional leading icon.
chunks.logic: One primary action per view centers decision-making and prevents competing calls to attention.
chunks.when_to_use: Primary task completion and high-value progress steps.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Secondary choices or low-impact options.
chunks.trade_offs: Multiple primary actions on the same surface compete and cancel each other out. Demote secondary actions to a button group or overflow menu.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Limit to one primary action per focal region to keep neural clarity in dense interfaces.

chunks.title: Switch Control
chunks.structure: Pill-shaped container with 2–4 equal-width segments; active segment has filled background and brand color.
chunks.logic: Segmented controls signal that options are mutually exclusive and equally weighted — not sequential steps.
chunks.when_to_use: List, grid, graph and other tightly related perspectives.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Cross-domain navigation or destination changes.
chunks.trade_offs: For more than 4 options a dropdown or tab bar scales better. Long labels break the visual balance of equal-weight segments.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Keep label lengths balanced to prevent perceptual jitter during transitions.

chunks.title: Global FAB
chunks.structure: Circular or squircle button, 56px minimum touch target, floating above content at bottom-right with drop shadow.
chunks.logic: The FAB occupies screen real estate at all times, so the action it triggers must justify that persistent cost.
chunks.when_to_use: Creation flows that are always relevant in the current surface.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Nested details or contextual subtasks.
chunks.trade_offs: FABs on desktop feel incongruous without a mobile companion. On desktop, prefer a toolbar button or inline primary action.
chunks.aetheris_insight: The FAB should feel like the source of creation in the system, not just another button.

chunks.title: Contextual Menu
chunks.structure: Three-dot or chevron trigger revealing a dropdown list. Destructive action sits last with color separation.
chunks.logic: Contextual menus preserve visual cleanliness by hiding low-frequency actions behind a trigger only those who need them will discover.
chunks.when_to_use: Rows, cards, assets and records with optional actions.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Primary flows that deserve direct visibility.
chunks.trade_offs: Hiding all actions makes the surface feel inert. Expose the most-used action as a direct affordance and reserve the menu for the rest.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Destructive actions should always sit last and visually separated from safe actions.

chunks.title: System Alerts
chunks.structure: Full-width or modal banner with semantic icon, severity color, headline and optional CTA button.
chunks.logic: Alerts interrupt the user's flow — use only when ignoring the state costs more than the interruption itself.
chunks.when_to_use: Critical system states, outages and blocked synchronization.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Informational or dismissible status changes.
chunks.trade_offs: Alert overuse causes alert blindness. Reserve for truly critical states — use toasts for everything else.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Alerts should break focus only when the cost of ignoring them exceeds the interruption.

chunks.title: Toast Notification
chunks.structure: Compact floating card, bottom-center or top-right, auto-dismissing in 3–5s with optional manual dismiss.
chunks.logic: Toasts confirm system behavior without requiring user action — they close themselves to preserve flow.
chunks.when_to_use: Saved, copied, synced or completed actions.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Anything requiring a user decision or persistent context.
chunks.trade_offs: If the message requires action or persists beyond 5s, it is not a toast — use an alert or modal instead.
chunks.aetheris_insight: If the user needs to act, it is not a toast. It is an interruption and should be treated as one.

chunks.title: Skeleton Loader
chunks.structure: Animated gray blocks matching the geometry of the incoming content — not a generic spinner.
chunks.logic: Skeletons set spatial expectations before content arrives, reducing perceived latency by anchoring the layout.
chunks.when_to_use: Async panels, lazy content, pagination and API-backed cards.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Operations so fast that the placeholder flickers.
chunks.trade_offs: If content loads in under 300ms, the skeleton flickers and creates more disruption than it prevents. Use a simple opacity fade instead.
chunks.aetheris_insight: A skeleton must mimic the final geometry; otherwise reveal feels like layout instability.

chunks.title: Metrics Plot
chunks.structure: Line or area chart with labeled axes, hover tooltips and optional reference lines for goals or targets.
chunks.logic: Temporal data is about direction and rate of change, not just the current value — a chart answers both simultaneously.
chunks.when_to_use: Velocity, KPI evolution and forecasted movement.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Single bounded values that need no trend context.
chunks.trade_offs: For a single current value without trend relevance, a metric card is clearer and less visually heavy than a chart.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Direction of change is often more actionable than the raw number itself.

chunks.title: Bioluminescent Heatmap
chunks.structure: Grid or canvas with luminance-based color scale from muted to vivid. Legend is mandatory.
chunks.logic: Color intensity maps frequency or density to spatial position, making clusters visible at a glance without counting.
chunks.when_to_use: Activity clusters, dependency hotspots and risk density.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Sparse datasets with few meaningful concentrations.
chunks.trade_offs: With sparse data, few cells have meaningful intensity — the visual becomes noise. Minimum viable density is roughly 10% cell coverage.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Map intensity with luminance and opacity before relying on hue shifts.

chunks.title: Radial Gauge
chunks.structure: Arc from 0 to maximum value with indicator fill; current value shown numerically in center.
chunks.logic: A radial form implies a maximum and minimum, making it semantically appropriate only for bounded values.
chunks.when_to_use: Health metrics, readiness scores and bounded KPIs.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Unbounded values or raw totals.
chunks.trade_offs: For multiple bounded values, a bar chart is denser and more comparable. Gauges are best used in isolation or pairs.
chunks.aetheris_insight: A radial gauge implies a maximum; never use it for values without clear bounds.

chunks.title: Sparkline Strip
chunks.structure: Micro line chart, 60–120px wide, no axes or labels, optionally color-coded by direction.
chunks.logic: Sparklines convey directionality — up, down or flat — in minimal space alongside a metric label.
chunks.when_to_use: Dense dashboards that still need directional context.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Situations where precise reading beats glanceability.
chunks.trade_offs: Sparklines sacrifice precision for compactness. If the user needs exact values at each point, use a full chart.
chunks.aetheris_insight: A sparkline answers one critical question fast: is this getting better or worse?

chunks.title: Entity Graph
chunks.structure: Nodes as entities, edges as relationships, with optional labels, direction arrows and weight encoding.
chunks.logic: Node-link diagrams reveal structural relationships that tabular data cannot express — adjacency is data.
chunks.when_to_use: Connected entities where adjacency itself is meaningful.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Linear flows better expressed as steps or trees.
chunks.trade_offs: Graphs with more than ~50 nodes become visually cluttered. Use filtering, clustering or a matrix view instead.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Relationships are also data, and surfacing them often reveals the true bottleneck.

chunks.title: Neural Input
chunks.structure: Full-width text field with subtle glow animation on focus, placeholder as contextual prompt, optional trailing action button.
chunks.logic: A semantically rich input field signals that the system accepts open-ended, natural-language queries — not just form values.
chunks.when_to_use: Search, prompts, generative commands and AI-assisted actions.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Rigid structured forms with heavy validation.
chunks.trade_offs: Neural inputs imply AI processing behind them. If the backend is a simple search, this styling creates a trust mismatch.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Subtle glow and focused contrast make the field feel alive without reducing legibility.

chunks.title: Selection Chips
chunks.structure: Pill-shaped labels, horizontally scrollable or wrapping, with filled and outlined states for selected and unselected.
chunks.logic: Chips make multi-select options tangible and show selected state inline, reducing the overhead of hidden dropdowns.
chunks.when_to_use: Status, labels, dataset refinement and filtering.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Long option lists that demand search or hierarchy.
chunks.trade_offs: Beyond 10–12 options, chips become unwieldy. Use a searchable multi-select dropdown instead.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Chips work best when options are few, semantically clear and visually balanced.

chunks.title: Gradient Slider
chunks.structure: Horizontal track with draggable thumb, gradient fill from left to thumb, current value label above or beside.
chunks.logic: A continuous slider is appropriate when the user needs to feel a range, not just select a discrete value.
chunks.when_to_use: Precision values with immediate visual response.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Discrete, categorical choices.
chunks.trade_offs: Sliders are hard to target precisely on touch. For exact numeric input, pair with a text field or step buttons.
chunks.aetheris_insight: A slider should communicate range, not ambiguity. Show the current value clearly.

chunks.title: Toggle Switch
chunks.structure: Pill track with circular thumb. Off state muted, on state in brand color. Label always visible.
chunks.logic: Toggles communicate binary state with an immediate effect — the UI changes the moment the switch moves.
chunks.when_to_use: Instant, reversible preferences.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Dangerous actions or changes that require confirmation.
chunks.trade_offs: For settings that require a save action before taking effect, use a checkbox with a Save button instead.
chunks.aetheris_insight: A toggle promises immediate reversibility; never use it for high-risk consequences.

chunks.title: Date Picker
chunks.structure: Trigger input showing formatted date, popover calendar with month navigation and day selection grid.
chunks.logic: Calendars anchor temporal choices in the user's mental model of weeks and months — more reliable than raw text input.
chunks.when_to_use: Scheduling, planning and time filtering.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Simple year or text inputs where a calendar is excessive.
chunks.trade_offs: For entering a well-known date, a text field is faster. Calendars add overhead when the user already knows the exact date.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Today should always be a visible anchor so the user can orient instantly.

chunks.title: Search Command Bar
chunks.structure: Modal overlay triggered by keyboard shortcut (⌘K), fuzzy search input, grouped results list with icons.
chunks.logic: Command bars give power users a keyboard-driven shortcut to any action without mouse navigation through menus.
chunks.when_to_use: Apps with broad IA, many actions or expert workflows.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Tiny products where every action is already visible.
chunks.trade_offs: Command bars require discovery — users must know they exist. Pair with an onboarding nudge or visible keyboard shortcut label.
chunks.aetheris_insight: A great command bar is not an accessory; it becomes the operational backbone.

chunks.title: Explanation Bubble
chunks.structure: Expandable card attached to a prediction or recommendation, showing rationale in 2–3 plain-language sentences.
chunks.logic: When AI drives a recommendation, the reasoning must accompany the output — otherwise trust cannot be calibrated by the user.
chunks.when_to_use: Any AI-driven score or recommendation shown to non-technical users.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Expert surfaces where raw coefficients matter more than summary language.
chunks.trade_offs: Explanation text that is too long defeats its purpose. Aim for 2–3 sentences covering what, why and confidence level.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Explanation depth should adapt to role: managers need actionability, engineers need detail.

chunks.title: Confidence Meter
chunks.structure: Progress bar, arc or numeric percentage with semantic color coding (green, amber, red tiers).
chunks.logic: Displaying confidence calibrates user reliance — high confidence invites action, low confidence invites verification.
chunks.when_to_use: Predictions, forecasts and probabilistic suggestions.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Deterministic rules where confidence is misleading theater.
chunks.trade_offs: A miscalibrated confidence score is worse than no score — it creates false certainty. Validate calibration before shipping.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Trust in AI is earned through uncertainty disclosure, not through tone of certainty.

chunks.title: Predictive Progress Card
chunks.structure: Card split between solid (actual) and dashed (projected) sections, with delta label showing days ahead or behind.
chunks.logic: Combining current state with projected trajectory gives managers the information they need to intervene before problems materialize.
chunks.when_to_use: Sprints, milestones and delivery tracking with historical signal.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Tasks with insufficient historical evidence.
chunks.trade_offs: Projections without sufficient historical data are unreliable. Require at least 2–3 completed sprints before activating.
chunks.aetheris_insight: The projection shadow must read as hypothesis, not promise, through muted styling.

chunks.title: Source Attribution Link
chunks.structure: Inline chip or footnote linking to the source document, log or dataset that powered the AI output.
chunks.logic: Provenance turns an assertion into evidence — it allows users to verify claims and builds durable trust in the system.
chunks.when_to_use: Every AI-generated summary, prediction or recommendation.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Pure UI feedback that is not data-derived.
chunks.trade_offs: If the source is a black-box third-party model output, attribution cannot be honest. Surface this limitation explicitly.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Explainability without provenance is storytelling. Evidence makes it auditable.

chunks.title: Dashboard
chunks.structure: Centralized telemetry hub with high-density data visualization and contextual action bars.
chunks.logic: Aggregation of disparate data sources into a unified cognitive plane.
chunks.context_of_use: Monitoring systems, complex SaaS management, and resource oversight.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Simple task-focused tools or mobile-first consumer apps where focus is singular.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Dashboards should breathe. In complex environments, prioritize temporal data: what is happening now over what has happened.

chunks.title: Multi-step Form
chunks.structure: Input fields fragmented into thematic logical blocks, each scoped to a single decision or data group, with persistent progress indication.
chunks.logic: Reduces overwhelm by sequencing decisions and maintaining momentum through completion.
chunks.context_of_use: Account registration, checkout flows, complex configuration wizards and onboarding sequences with branching logic.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Simple forms under five fields, related inputs that benefit from simultaneous visibility or quick mobile actions.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Focus on momentum. Use predictive pre-fills and inline validation to eliminate cognitive drag between steps.

chunks.title: Onboarding
chunks.structure: Progressive disclosure sequence that introduces key features through contextual education without interrupting the primary workflow.
chunks.context_of_use: First-run experiences, post-signup activation, feature discovery after major updates and role-based capability reveals.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Interfaces that are already self-evident, transactional flows or returning users who already completed setup.
chunks.trade_offs: Increases activation and adoption, but becomes easy to skip if it feels generic or detached from user intent.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Personalize the path. Show users what they care about first instead of replaying a generic tour.

Show users what they care about first instead of replaying a generic tour.

chunks.title: Data Explorer
chunks.structure: Dynamic filtering interface with faceted search, drill-down capabilities and cross-dimensional analysis controls over large datasets.
chunks.logic: Hypothesis-driven exploration where users define queries and the system surfaces relevant subsets.
chunks.context_of_use: Analytics platforms, research tools, inventory systems and BI dashboards with multi-dimensional data.
chunks.trade_offs: Extremely powerful for experts, but needs clear affordances, sane defaults and saved views to avoid novice overload.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Use semantic search as the primary entry point. A single natural-language query often replaces a chain of manual filters.

chunks.title: Empty States
chunks.structure: Intentional placeholder view combining explanation, hierarchy and one primary action scoped to the empty container.
chunks.logic: Transforms absence into guidance, turning the first interaction with a feature into a conversion moment.
chunks.context_of_use: New accounts, cleared tables, zero-result searches, unconnected integrations and fresh projects.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Transient loading or background processing, where skeleton screens preserve spatial continuity better.
chunks.trade_offs: Excellent for orientation and activation, but weakens trust if it feels decorative instead of actionable.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Treat void as opportunity. A clear next step reframes incompleteness as a starting point, not a failure.

chunks.title: Settings & Config
chunks.logic: Hierarchical nesting of system variables and user preferences.
chunks.context_of_use: Global application control, preferences, permissions and environment-level tuning.
chunks.trade_offs: Powerful and expected, but quickly becomes hostile when high-impact toggles are buried too deep.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Configuration is the user's manifesto. Never hide high-impact toggles behind more than two layers of navigation.

Never hide high-impact toggles behind more than two layers of navigation.

chunks.title: Command Center
chunks.structure: Single-input, modal-driven command surface backed by keyboard shortcuts and semantic matching.
chunks.trade_offs: Fastest pattern for experts, but almost invisible to new users without clear onboarding or discoverability cues.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Language is the most efficient interface. Every complex app benefits from a text-based shortcut system.

chunks.title: Focus Mode
chunks.structure: A modal or full-screen overlay that isolates a single artifact by collapsing sidebars, notifications and peripheral navigation.
chunks.logic: Eliminates context switching cost and lowers the cognitive price of sustaining attention on one objective.
chunks.context_of_use: Long-form editors, code reviews, document drafting and design canvases that need prolonged immersion.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Workflows that depend on simultaneous references, multi-pane awareness or live collaborative context.
chunks.trade_offs: Maximizes concentration and quality, but can disorient users if returning to the broader interface is high-friction.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Silence is a design decision. A good Focus Mode curates attention instead of merely hiding controls.

chunks.title: Collaboration
chunks.structure: Real-time presence indicators, conflict-resolution UI and co-editing primitives layered onto an existing single-user interface.
chunks.logic: Operational transformation or CRDT-based synchronization turns presence into first-class interface data.
chunks.context_of_use: Collaborative documents, shared canvases, code review sessions and whiteboarding workflows.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Strict sequential ownership flows, low-latency environments with tight constraints or single-user personal surfaces.
chunks.trade_offs: Increases team velocity, but adds significant system complexity and can introduce visual noise in solo tasks.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Presence is data. Show what others are editing, not only where they are.

chunks.title: Timeline
chunks.structure: Chronological log of state mutations, user actions or system events with actor identity, timestamps and restore affordances.
chunks.logic: Treats every meaningful change as an immutable event, turning time into a navigable axis.
chunks.context_of_use: Version-controlled editors, audit logs, publishing workflows and configuration history surfaces.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Ephemeral live feeds, trivial interactions or cases where event storage costs outweigh user value.
chunks.trade_offs: Builds recovery confidence and trust, but needs careful abstraction to avoid overwhelming non-technical users.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Permanent history is more than undo. It gives users permission to take creative risks.

chunks.title: Entity Picker
chunks.structure: Inline or popover search-driven selector for relational entities with type-ahead, multi-select and preview chips.
chunks.logic: Creates typed references instead of duplicating data, preserving authority in the source context.
chunks.context_of_use: Assignees, tags, mentions, attachments, relationship fields and permission scope selectors.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Small static option sets or flat values such as booleans, enums and simple colors.
chunks.trade_offs: Preserves relational integrity and reduces duplication, but relies on fast backend search and responsive type-ahead UX.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Link, don't copy. References preserve authority and allow the system to reason about relationships.

chunks.title: Color Tokens
chunks.structure: Primary scale (#f5f0ff → #4a1aa0) + Surface scale (#000000 → #2c2c2f)
chunks.logic: Primary tokens drive brand identity and interactive states. Surface tokens define depth hierarchy.
chunks.context_of_use: Every component that uses color must reference these tokens, never raw hex values.
chunks.when_to_use: Use primary-200 (#deccfd) for brand accent, primary-300 (#c2a0fc) for secondary. Use background (#0e0e10) for app background, surface-container (#19191c) for cards.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Never use raw hex values outside this token system.
chunks.aetheris_insight: primary-200 and primary-300 form the signature gradient. Surface tokens create depth without shadows.
chunks.text: AETHERIS COLOR TOKENS | Primary Scale: primary-50: #f5f0ff, primary-100: #ede2ff, primary-200: #deccfd, primary-300: #c2a0fc, primary-400: #a777f9, primary-500: #8b4ff5, primary-600: #6a30d4, primary-700: #4a1aa0 | Surface Scale: surface-lowest: #000000, background: #0e0e10, surface-container-low: #131315, surface-container: #19191c, surface-container-high: #1f1f22, surface-container-highest: #262528, surface-bright: #2c2c2f

chunks.title: Semantic Color Tokens
chunks.structure: Named semantic roles mapped to hex values
chunks.logic: Semantic tokens abstract color intent from raw values.
chunks.context_of_use: Use semantic tokens (--aetheris-color-primary, --aetheris-color-error) for states and feedback.
chunks.when_to_use: Use error (#ff6e84) for destructive actions and alerts. Use success (#7ee787) for confirmations.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Do not use warning color for primary actions.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Semantic tokens decouple meaning from aesthetics — changing a theme only requires updating token values.
chunks.text: AETHERIS SEMANTIC COLOR TOKENS | Primary (--aetheris-color-primary): #deccfd | Secondary (--aetheris-color-secondary): #c2a0fc | Success (--aetheris-color-success): #7ee787 | Warning (--aetheris-color-warning): #ffa657 | Error (--aetheris-color-error): #ff6e84

chunks.title: Typography Tokens
chunks.structure: display-xl → heading-lg → body-md → label-sm
chunks.logic: Four-level type scale balancing display impact with readable body density.
chunks.context_of_use: Every text element should reference one of these four scales.
chunks.when_to_use: display-xl for hero headlines, heading-lg for section anchors, body-md for documentation, label-sm for metadata and chips.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Do not mix custom font sizes outside this scale.
chunks.aetheris_insight: A constrained type scale is invisible when correct and jarring when broken.
chunks.text: AETHERIS TYPOGRAPHY TOKENS | display-xl (text-6xl font-black tracking-tighter): Hero headlines and identity surfaces | heading-lg (text-3xl font-black tracking-tight): Major sections and content anchors | body-md (text-base leading-7 text-on-surface-variant): Documentation, explanations and descriptions | label-sm (text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-[0.24em] text-on-surface-variant): Metadata, compact navigation and chips

chunks.title: Spacing Tokens
chunks.structure: space-1 (0.25rem) through space-10 (2.5rem)
chunks.logic: Consistent rhythm across all layout decisions.
chunks.context_of_use: All padding, margin and gap values should use these tokens.
chunks.when_to_use: space-4 (1rem) for default card padding, space-6 for section blocks, space-10 for hero separation.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Do not use arbitrary pixel values for spacing.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Consistent spacing is what makes dense interfaces feel intentional rather than cramped.
chunks.text: AETHERIS SPACING TOKENS | space-1 (0.25rem): micro alignment and icon breathing room | space-2 (0.5rem): compact group spacing and chips | space-4 (1rem): default card padding and form rhythm | space-6 (1.5rem): section blocks and content density | space-10 (2.5rem): hero spacing and layout separation

chunks.title: Side Drawer vs Modal Overlay
chunks.structure: Decision tree based on user focus requirements
chunks.logic: Spatial continuity vs. attention isolation trade-off.
chunks.context_of_use: Any form, panel or overlay interaction that requires choosing a container type.
chunks.when_to_use: Side Drawer: user needs page context. Modal: action requires full focus.
chunks.when_not_to_use: Do not use Modal for low-stakes, reversible actions that don't need interruption.
chunks.trade_offs: Visual occlusion with drawers; modal blindness and context loss with modals.
chunks.aetheris_insight: The decision maps to one question: does the user need to see the page while acting?
chunks.text: AETHERIS DESIGN DECISION: Side Drawer vs Modal Overlay | Logic: Side Drawer preserves spatial context — use when user needs to reference content behind. Modal Overlay demands full attention — use for confirmations, creation flows, critical alerts. | When to Use Side Drawer: High density content, persistent context, form step integration. | When to Use Modal: Actions requiring undivided focus, confirmations, blocking decisions. | Trade-offs: Visual occlusion (drawer), contextual drift (modal blindness). | Aetheris Insight: If the user needs page context, use a drawer. If undivided attention is needed, use a modal.

chunks.title: Primary vs. Secondary Button Logic
chunks.logic: When to use the signature gradient versus restrained secondary treatments for terminal actions.

chunks.title: List vs. Bento
chunks.logic: List layout excels for scannable, sequential data with consistent row density. Bento grid excels for heterogeneous content where size encodes priority — larger cells signal higher importance. Use List when users compare items row by row. Use Bento when visual hierarchy and content variety matter more than strict alignment. Trade-off: Bento requires more design effort per item; List is faster to implement but less expressive.

chunks.title: Haptic Feedback
chunks.logic: Haptic feedback confirms high-stakes or irreversible actions on mobile — deletes, confirmations and state toggles. Reserve for moments where tactile confirmation reduces user anxiety about permanence. When to use: destructive actions, form submissions, binary state changes. When not to use: passive events, informational toasts, decorative interactions. Trade-off: overuse degrades trust and drains battery; underuse leaves users uncertain after consequential actions.

chunks.title: Confidence Metrics
chunks.structure: Three-axis scoring: Recommendation clarity, Token consistency, UX principle fit
chunks.logic: Scores surface how well a recommendation aligns with design system rules and UX principles.
chunks.context_of_use: Shown after oracle responses to help users calibrate trust
chunks.when_to_use: Reference when evaluating competing recommendations
chunks.trade_offs: Scores are proxies — high similarity does not guarantee the correct recommendation for every context.
chunks.aetheris_insight: Confidence calibration is what distinguishes an oracle from a search engine.

chunks.title: Decision Alternatives
chunks.structure: Multiple paths evaluated; only the best-fit strategy is returned
chunks.logic: Alternative paths are weighted against clarity, rationale depth and trust calibration.
chunks.context_of_use: Internal oracle evaluation — surfaces in XAI explanation when requested
chunks.when_to_use: Reference when the user asks why a specific response style was chosen
chunks.trade_offs: Showing rejected paths increases transparency but adds cognitive load.
chunks.aetheris_insight: The best oracle response is the one the user can audit, trust, and reuse.
chunks.text: AETHERIS REASONING: Decision Alternatives | Logic: Beatrice evaluates multiple response strategies before selecting one | Flat rule response: Rejected: too prescriptive and low on explanation | Documentation dump: Rejected: high cognitive load and weak prioritization | Layered oracle guidance: Selected: best balance of clarity, rationale and trust

chunks.title: Persona Goals — Francisco Soares
chunks.logic: Goals define what the primary consumer persona needs from Beatrice.
chunks.context_of_use: Primary persona: Product Manager, mid-level DS consumer, sprint-pressure context
chunks.when_to_use: Reference when designing oracle responses for time-constrained users
chunks.aetheris_insight: Francisco wants the right answer in 30 seconds — depth on demand, not by default.
chunks.text: AETHERIS PERSONA: Francisco Soares — Goals | Context Of Use: Primary consumer persona — Product Manager using the design system | Instant answer, without manual searching: Ask in natural language and get the component name plus rationale in seconds, without opening tabs or navigating multiple sections. | Fast decision without depending on design: Resolve component doubts alone, during a sprint or meeting, without waiting for outside validation. | Fast team alignment: Ensure designers and developers make the same decision and reduce rework caused by divergent interpretation. | Enough confidence to decide and move forward: He does not need absolute certainty; he needs calibrated confidence to proceed without revisiting the issue later.

chunks.title: Persona Frustrations — Francisco Soares
chunks.logic: Documented friction points that the oracle must address.
chunks.context_of_use: Guides oracle response design: answers must be fast, scannable and source-backed
chunks.when_to_use: Reference when evaluating whether an oracle response resolves the user's real barrier
chunks.aetheris_insight: The oracle exists to eliminate the gap between documentation and decision.
chunks.text: AETHERIS PERSONA: Francisco Soares — Frustrations | Context Of Use: Pain points that Beatrice is designed to resolve | Long documentation with no contextual guidance: He needs to read many pages for an answer that should arrive in seconds, which does not fit sprint pace. | Inconsistency across team members: The same guideline can be read in different ways, generating variation and misalignment. | Ad hoc solutions outside the system: When the answer does not arrive fast, the team improvises or pushes the decision to someone else. | Does not know where to start in a new product: When starting from scratch, there is no guidance on component combinations, screen structure or the principles behind choices. | Validation always depends on another human: Even simple decisions end up depending on the design lead, creating a bottleneck he sees as unacceptable.

chunks.title: Framework Support
chunks.structure: npm packages: @aetheris/core, @aetheris/tokens, @aetheris/react
chunks.logic: Aetheris ships framework-specific adapters alongside a framework-agnostic core.
chunks.context_of_use: Setting up Aetheris in a new or existing project

chunks.when_not_to_use: Do not import @aetheris/react in a Vue project or vice versa.
chunks.trade_offs: Framework packages add a thin adapter layer — minimal overhead, maximum type safety.
chunks.aetheris_insight: The core + tokens separation means theme changes never require framework updates.
